title: GIFT Nifty Signals Weak Open for Sensex, Nifty as Crude Stays Above $114
excerpt: GIFT Nifty futures fell 0.39 per cent early Thursday after the Sensex closed at 73,246.03 and the Nifty at 22,698.85, with the Fed on hold, Brent at $114.63 and Asian markets split.
body:
• GIFT Nifty futures traded at 22,662.50 early Thursday, down 89.50 points or 0.39 per cent, signalling a flat-to-weak open for the Sensex and Nifty 50 on October 29.
  • On Wednesday the Sensex closed at 73,246.03, down 352.64 points or 0.48 per cent, and the Nifty 50 ended at 22,698.85, down 50.90 points or 0.22 per cent.
  • The US Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75 to 4 per cent by a 10-2 vote, with two members favouring a hike; Brent crude stayed elevated at $114.63 a barrel.
  • For traders: Nifty support sits at 22,500, with resistance at 22,800-22,830; foreign investors bought Rs 871.83 crore of shares on Wednesday and domestic institutions Rs 643.35 crore.

Indian equities face a cautious start on Thursday, October 29, with GIFT Nifty futures pointing lower even as Wall Street closed higher after the US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady. The November GIFT Nifty contract was quoted at 22,662.50 at 8:11 a.m. IST, down 89.50 points or 0.39 per cent from its previous close and at a discount to the Nifty 50's Wednesday close of 22,698.85, according to HDFC Sky. Upstox put the futures at 22,682, down 96 points, while Reuters reported GIFT Nifty at 22,708 earlier in the morning, indicating a muted start.

Where the benchmarks closed

On Wednesday, the BSE Sensex fell 352.64 points, or 0.48 per cent, to close at 73,246.03, and the NSE Nifty 50 declined 50.90 points, or 0.22 per cent, to 22,698.85. IT and oil and gas stocks led the losses, with the Nifty IT and Nifty Oil & Gas indices each down about 2 per cent and Infosys, HCL Technologies, Reliance Industries and ONGC among the laggards. Auto, consumer durables, media and pharma indices rose about 1 per cent each, and broader markets outperformed, with the Nifty Midcap index up 0.4 per cent and the Nifty Smallcap index up 0.9 per cent. Reuters noted the benchmarks have fallen in six of the last seven sessions as elevated oil prices raised concerns over inflation, interest rates and the rupee.

Global cues: Wall Street up, Asia split

US stocks ended higher on Wednesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.19 per cent to 52,475.10, the S&P 500 rose 0.28 per cent to 7,743.98 and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.27 per cent to 26,549.85. After the close, however, heavy cash burn at Alphabet sent its shares 10 per cent lower in after-hours trading and drove Nasdaq futures about 1 per cent lower, while Microsoft rose 3 per cent on better-than-expected cash flows, Reuters reported via Upstox.

Asian markets were mixed on Thursday morning. Japan's Nikkei advanced 0.32 per cent and Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained 0.2 per cent, while China's Shanghai Composite declined 0.62 per cent and South Korea's Kospi dropped 2.13 per cent, according to Upstox. HDFC Sky put the Kospi's fall at 2.39 per cent to 5,868.66, with Taiwan down 1.42 per cent, while Malaysia, Singapore and Australia advanced.

Fed hold, oil and flows

The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.75 to 4 per cent on Wednesday, as expected, but two of the 12 voting members wanted an immediate 25 basis point hike, and the central bank described inflation as elevated. Markets now price in about an 85 per cent chance of a December hike, according to HDFC Sky. That keeps higher US yields competing with emerging-market equities for capital, Reuters noted.

Crude remains the other pressure point. Brent eased 0.60 per cent to $114.63 a barrel on Thursday and WTI fell 1.01 per cent to $101.74, after Brent climbed above $115 on Wednesday following a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery. For India, a major crude importer, sustained prices above $110 mean a bigger import bill and continued pressure on the rupee and inflation.

Flows offered some support. Foreign institutional investors bought shares worth Rs 871.83 crore on Wednesday, a second consecutive session of buying, and domestic institutional investors purchased Rs 643.35 crore, although foreign investors have still offloaded $3.74 billion worth of shares so far in October, according to Reuters.

Levels and earnings to watch

Technical levels frame the session: the Nifty's 22,500 level is an important near-term support, while 22,800-22,830 is the key resistance zone, with a sustained breakout opening the way towards 23,000. The Sensex faces resistance around 73,500-73,800, with support at 72,600-73,000. Earnings will drive stock-specific moves: about 150 companies are scheduled to report September-quarter results on Thursday, including Asian Paints, Coal India, Trent and InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo), according to the BSE list cited by Upstox.
